content.text: {"concept_key":"c6-science-evaporation","title":"Evaporation","quick":"Evaporation is when liquid water turns into invisible water vapour due to heat, and rises into air. It happens slowly, at any temperature, only from the surface.","full":"Think of wet clothes drying on a terrace in the sun. The water in the clothes doesn't boil, but slowly disappears into the air as vapour because the sun's heat gives water molecules energy to escape from the surface. Same thing happens with seas and rivers: sun heats the top surface of water, some water turns into vapour (gas form, invisible) and rises up into the sky. What stays same: it is still water, just a different form (gas instead of liquid). What differs: evaporation is slow and happens only at the surface, unlike boiling which is fast and happens throughout the liquid.","traps":["Confusing evaporation with boiling","Thinking vapour is visible like steam or fog","Forgetting that evaporation happens only at the surface, not inside the liquid"],"misconception":"Child thinks water 'disappears' completely instead of turning into invisible vapour that goes into the air.","parent_questions":[{"q":"What happens to wet clothes on the terrace by evening?","expected_answer_hint":"The water in them evaporates due to sun's heat and becomes vapour in the air."},{"q":"Is water vapour something we can see?","expected_answer_hint":"No, it is invisible gas; what we see as clouds/fog is tiny water droplets, not vapour itself."}],"check_question":{"q":"A puddle of water on the road disappears after a sunny day. What happened to the water?","options":["It evaporated into water vapour","It froze into ice","It turned into mud"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct!
